settings.title: Sized to your network, not built around ours.

settings.editor: The four pillars of an Apical partnership, the rollout phases we run from, and the framework we use when we sit down to write the terms. Specifics are scoped to your robot count, geography, and payer mix during the first consult.
PillarsRolloutTermsFitNext stepsFAQ

THE MODEL

Per-case alignment
over capex.

Apical avoids putting hardware capex on the practice. The default structure is a per-case fee or a lease that scales with how often the platform is actually used. The specific number is set during the consult, against your case mix.

THE OVERSIGHT

A licensed clinician
on every loop.

Every robot has a supervising specialist on the case. Panel composition, coverage hours, and escalation paths are scoped to your case windows and documented in the partnership doc — not promised generically on a landing page.

THE ROLLOUT

Flagship → cluster
→ network.

Start in one or two flagship robots with full Apical support on-site. Expand to a regional cluster once the flagship metrics hold. Move to network-wide rollout when the math and the workflow are both steady. Pace is yours, not ours.

THE EXIT

Annual renewal,
no multi-year lock-in.

The partnership is structured so you can step out at the next annual renewal if it is not working. Hardware comes back to us. We stay honest; you stay flexible. Specific notice periods and end-of-term conditions are written into the contract, not the brochure.

settings.title: The path from first email to first chair.

settings.editor:
Intro call · 30 minutes

Clinical director and CFO on the line. We confirm robot count, geography, payer mix, and which specialty channel is leaking. We do not pitch the platform yet — we listen for whether the partnership shape we offer can even match what you need.

WHENWithin 5 business days

Custom revenue model · written

Apical returns a per-location revenue model built against your case mix and payer reality, with the phased rollout plan attached. You see the math before any contract language is exchanged. If the math doesn't clear, we say so and end here — no follow-up sequence.

WHEN5 business days after intro

Clinical-lab walkthrough

Your clinical lead spends a half-day in Dr. Lewis's lab. The bench platforms run live. You meet the supervising specialist panel candidates for your case windows. Apical never asks for a signature on this trip — the visit is for diligence, not closing.

WHEN2–3 weeks after model

Partnership doc · drafted to your terms

We write the partnership contract against the seven questions on the framework above. Your counsel marks it up. The exit terms, liability split, and SLA are settled before we discuss start dates. Annual renewal is the default — no multi-year lock-in.

WHENCounsel pace

Flagship robot · live

Apical embeds on-site with the supervising specialist. One robot. Full Apical coverage until the practice clinicians are cleared at the supervisor's pace. Weekly metrics review with you and your CFO. The Cluster stage only opens when the flagship data clears.

WHENTargeted within 90 days of signing
WHAT WE GET ASKED

settings.title: The five hardest questions DSO operators ask us — and the answers we give before we sign.

settings.editor:
How does this avoid becoming another vendor that wastes our clinicians' time?

Two ways. One: the intro call is 30 minutes with your clinical director and CFO — not a six-week discovery dance. If the partnership shape doesn't match what you need, we end the conversation on that call. Two: Apical is on-site for the full flagship rollout. We absorb the clinician hours required to get the first chair clean; you don't subsidise the integration.

What does this actually cost us per location, and where is the capex?

Leases start at $3,667/mo per robot, plus consumables billed separately through the approved supply system. Final price varies by the functions you configure for each robot, so two networks rarely land on the same number. There is no hardware capex on the practice — the robot runs on a lease, not a purchase. Consumables price varies by case mix and is scoped during the consult.

How does this interact with our existing referral network and specialist relationships?

Apical is built to keep cases in-network that were leaking to outside specialists. Your existing referral relationships stay intact for everything outside the deployed channel. We don't compete with your trusted specialists — we equip the chairs that have been bleeding cases to them.

What's the exit story if this doesn't work after the flagship?

The contract is annual. If the flagship metrics don't clear, you don't authorise the Cluster stage. At renewal you walk. Hardware comes back to us at our cost. The supervisor panel relationships stay with you if you want to keep working with them independently. No clawbacks, no transition fees, no integration penalty.

How are you different from the autonomous-robot startups raising rounds right now?

We're not selling you autonomy. We're selling supervised throughput with a licensed clinician on every loop, prescribed by a dentist who's been placing implants since 1981. The autonomous-robot pitch makes a better fundraising deck. The supervised-robot pitch makes a better dental practice.

Send us your robot count, geography, and current implant referral economics. We come back with a per-location revenue model and a phased rollout plan in five business days.
